notes.heading: How to read this page now: three verdicts, and why the distinction matters

table: The source of this word is deleted and has no replacement. It reads `0` because there is nothing behind it, **not** because nothing happened
Never read it as a measurement. A word that read a plausible value instead would be a defect -- "engine idle" and "no engine" must not be confusable
The register still reads back exactly what software wrote, but the value **no longer reaches the wire**
Writing it changes nothing observable. Do not infer from a successful readback that the setting took effect
Still real, now sourced from the protocol processor's class-D face instead of a deleted engine
Read it normally; the meaning is unchanged

the whole `0x700` TCAM group still stores; **nothing reads it** and the port is PROMISCUOUS
`0x72C LPF_CTRL` still RW with no filter behind it

**Reading the three failure modes** (listener bound, nothing accepted):

table: frames are not reaching the parser at all -- look upstream (MAC, filter, classify), not at the listener

table: upstream paused, four fed pairs (the shipping 1x1x8 lane)
upstream paused, 32 fed pairs (an 8x8 elaboration with the lane)
an unaligned packet grid against a disciplined peer (one slip per 1.958 s: INTERNAL before #629)
8.9 h on four pairs, 1.1 h on 32
35.6 h at one dup per slip; sooner when a wider marker dither adds dup/skip pairs

one grid: the packet grid follows the selected source and the upstream talker rides the same media clock. Under CRF a static `SLIP_TDM` is a talker that repeats and skips no TDM frame: the aligner holds the frame close 256 cycles off the walk's crossing at every settled lock phase (the guarded crossing above); an engagement's acquisition may add one dup and one skip, once
dups climbing 0.51/s per fed pair (about 2/s on the shipping four-pair lane, 16/s on 32 pairs)
dups minus skips climbing 0.51/s (dups alone at 0.51/s while the marker dithers over two adjacent cycles; a wider dither adds skips and as many extra dups)

the packet grid is not aligned to the front end: the -10.64 ppm plan. At INTERNAL this was the rule before #629; since #629 (A2-a) the aligner runs at every source, so on a current image look for a dead TDM feed (the aligner's watchdog disengages it)
our own front end is aligned but the upstream talker's clock is not this media clock: look at the peer's clock source

the half is spent: an upstream pause, cable pull or talker stop-without-unbind (a stopped front-end clock for `SLIP_TDM`) pegged it in under two seconds, and it says nothing about the present rate; a saturated word is not evidence of one grid. Reset to re-arm, then read again; a bind wipe un-primes the pair but does not clear the word

modules.heading: 0x8DC  -  render presentation state
modules.purpose: Presentation state of the selected listener.

table: Frames queued past the frame every interface has read: the newest frame the stream wrote, less that one; 0 with none queued; saturates at 255 (the queue is 128 frames deep at 48 kHz)
Interface 0's last read of the stream found no sample: before the stream's first presentation time, after it ends, or in a gap; level, no counter
The stream has presented a sample on every read for 100 ms running; level, no counter

Global count of PDUs with a refused event, once per PDU: late (an event at or before the frame every interface has read) or too early (an event beyond the queue). Each event is judged on its own frame, so a counted PDU's other events may still be presented; saturates at `0xFFFF`, never wraps

modules.heading: 0x920  -  protocol-processor control plane  `(KL_pp_shadow, VERSION major 2)`
modules.purpose: Protocol-processor control plane and the saved-state window.

table: **A restore genuinely completed**: the writer is live and the walk read records out of a validated image
**Blank media behind a validated image**: the store is real but held nothing this walk could use. Not a failure: Milan permits an entity that has never been bound

**Torn read-back, or a BLIND walk**: the walk aborted and the whole image was discarded, or at some cycle of the walk no validated image stood behind the device face, so what it read was the blank answer. The blind verdict is latched per walk in `KL_pp_shadow.sv`: validating the image after the walk does not restore anything, so it cannot clear it
**No writer has answered and the walk ran blind**: what a build whose firmware has not configured the backing store reports, `0x5B00_008C`

regions.rom: Boot ROM holding the bare-metal firmware image.
regions.sram: On-chip SRAM: the firmware's stack and data.
regions.milan_csr: The Milan CSR block this page documents.
regions.milan_flashboot_aem: Flash slot of the AEM entity image.
regions.milan_flash_journal: Flash slots of the saved-state journal (A and B); a reflash must not erase it.
regions.pp_window: The protocol processor's reserved main-memory window.
regions.pp_desc: AEM descriptor image, read by the processor.

csr_banks.ctrl: SoC control: reset, scratch, bus errors.
csr_banks.milan_mac: Milan MAC wrapper: PHY reset, MDIO, MAC counters, loopback, link status.
csr_banks.ppmem: Protocol-processor memory-bridge observers, pinned to the last CSR page.

soc_registers.ppmem_desc_req: descriptor-image read bridge: `[31:16]` accesses **ISSUED** (one per bus access, counted at its start, not per held cycle), `[15:0]` accesses the bus **ACKED** without `err`
soc_registers.ppmem_desc_fault: `[31:16]` accesses answered with **err**, `[15:0]` accesses the watchdog **abandoned** with no answer at all
soc_registers.ppmem_resp_req: AECP response-buffer read+write bridge, same two fields. This face writes as well as reads: a write that faults voids the response rather than putting a half-written one on the wire
soc_registers.ppmem_resp_fault: same two fields as `desc_fault`, for the response bridge
soc_registers.ppmem_stat: live state, not counts: `[0]` descriptor bridge **poisoned** (a timed-out access is still owed an answer; the next answer it collects is discarded), `[1]` descriptor bridge is driving `cyc`/`stb` **right now**, `[2]` response bridge poisoned, `[3]` response bridge driving `cyc`/`stb`, `[4]` the **LiteDRAM DFI hand-off has been seen** (see below), `[31:24]` constant presence tag `0x5B` -- the same tag as `PP_STAT`, and the register to read first: `0` here means the gateware predates this bank, which is otherwise indistinguishable from four zeroed counters
soc_registers.milan_mac_phy_crg_reset: PHY reset of the port the image is built for (`--eth-port`): the PHY clock/reset block's `_reset` storage, which drives the PHY reset pin. This is the PHY reset; `PHY_RESET` (0x11C) is inert. `ETH_GUARD` does not gate it at this head.
soc_registers.milan_mac_phy_mdio_w: Software bit-bang MDIO write register (clock, output enable, data).
soc_registers.milan_mac_core_preamble_crc: LiteEth status, reset 1: the MAC core inserts and checks preamble and CRC.
soc_registers.milan_mac_loopback: 1 = internal MAC TX to MAC RX loopback.
soc_registers.milan_mac_link_status: Link, speed and duplex published by firmware; mirrored into `MAC_STATUS` (0x110). Reset: link up, 1000 Mb/s on GMII (100 on MII), full duplex.

soc_notes.heading: Protocol-processor memory bridges (LiteX CSR bank, `0xf000f800`)
rows: **The verdict table.** Read `desc_req` and `desc_fault` (or the `resp_` pair) and compare:

table: the bridges are **held off the bus**: the BIOS has not handed the DFI back to the LiteDRAM controller yet, so both answer `err` without touching the bus. Expected between FPGA configuration and the end of `sdram_init`, and a standing `0` here means the BIOS never got that far
the bridge **never asked the bus**. The bus is not the fault: look at the processor's request face (`PP_DIAG` `0x930`, the side-port snapshot)
every access completed. If the image is still invalid the fault is upstream of the bus: the descriptor image itself, or its base
an access is **outstanding right now**. `stat[1]`/`stat[3]` say which face is still holding `cyc`/`stb`; it will become a `timed_out` when the watchdog expires
the interconnect answered `err` (LiteX raises `err` **with** `ack`, so a failed access is an answer, not a silence). A descriptor fetched this way is refused, never served
the access was **never answered** and the watchdog abandoned it. `stat[0]`/`stat[2]` show the master poisoned until the memory pays the answer it still owes

CLS_MAP.name: PCP to traffic-class map (scratch)
CLS_MAP.purpose: Retained PCP to traffic-class map; no logic reads it.

CLS_REGEN.name: Priority regeneration (scratch)
CLS_REGEN.purpose: Retained priority regeneration map; no logic reads it.

fields.CLS_REGEN: priority regeneration, 8×3 bits (ingress PCP→internal prio). Reset was `0x688FAC` until 2026-07-05 - a half-swap (0..3↔4..7) that misrouted every tagged SR frame; fixed to identity.

CLS_TCQ.name: Traffic-class to queue map (scratch)
CLS_TCQ.purpose: Retained traffic-class to queue map; no logic reads it.

fields.CLS_TCQ: TC→queue, 8×`ceil(log2 N)` bits. At `N`=5 that is still 3 bits/entry and the reset is the 5-queue map: TC0/1→q0, TC2→**q3** (SR class B), TC3→**q4** (SR class A), TC4/5→q1 (control), TC6/7→q2 (gPTP). Every queue is mapped -- there is no spare. An entry naming a queue ≥ `N` is **clamped to q0** by `traffic_class_map` (without the clamp `axis_demux` would silently drop the frame -- `select >= M_COUNT`); 5 is not a power of two either, so the clamp is still load-bearing.

PTP_ILAT.name: Ingress latency (scratch)
PTP_ILAT.purpose: Readable inert scratch; corrections are published at GPTP_LAT.

fields.PTP_ILAT: 🟡 **Readable, inert scratch since `0x0056`.** A read returns the last written value; no timestamp-correction consumer reads the word at this VERSION. The live owner since `0x005E` is the fabric gPTP plane, which applies its board's correction as an elaboration constant and publishes the applied pair at `GPTP_LAT` (`0x7F0`); this word stays scratch so the same correction cannot be applied by two owners (#358). Ingress latency correction, ns, that the `ptp_ts_core` RX tap **SUBTRACTED** from its captures; that tap is no longer instantiated

PTP_ELAT.name: Egress latency (scratch)
PTP_ELAT.purpose: Readable inert scratch; corrections are published at GPTP_LAT.

fields.PTP_ELAT: 🟡 **Readable, inert scratch since `0x0056`.** A read returns the last written value; no timestamp-correction consumer reads the word at this VERSION. The live owner since `0x005E` is the fabric gPTP plane, which applies its board's correction as an elaboration constant and publishes the applied pair at `GPTP_LAT` (`0x7F0`); this word stays scratch so the same correction cannot be applied by two owners (#358). Egress latency correction, ns, that the TX tap **ADDED**; that tap is no longer instantiated

PPS_CTRL.name: PPS alarm control
PPS_CTRL.purpose: PPS enable, arm strobe and the built capability bit.

PPS_TGLO.name: PPS target, low word
PPS_TGLO.purpose: Absolute PPS target to arm, bits 31 to 0.

PPS_TGHI.name: PPS target, high word
PPS_TGHI.purpose: Absolute PPS target to arm, bits 63 to 32.

PPS_RDLO.name: PPS live target, low word
PPS_RDLO.purpose: Target the PHC publishes back, bits 31 to 0.

PPS_RDHI.name: PPS live target, high word
PPS_RDHI.purpose: Target the PHC publishes back, bits 63 to 32.

PPS_WIDTH.name: PPS pulse width
PPS_WIDTH.purpose: PPS pulse width in PHC clock cycles.

fields.PPS_WIDTH: Pulse width in PHC clock **cycles**, not seconds: `width_s = PTP_PPS_WIDTH / f_PHC`, and `f_PHC` is the period `PTP_INCR` already reports. Elaborated as one millisecond of the datapath clock (`100 000` in the 100 MHz shape, `125 000` at the recommended 125 MHz). 0 when the comparator was not built

ADP_CTRL.name: ADP control
ADP_CTRL.purpose: Entity enable and the advertised valid time.

fields.ADP_ENABLE: advertise-enable -- **LIVE, and ORed with `PP_CTRL[0]` (`0x920`): either bit enables the entity**.
fields.ADP_VALID_TIME: valid_time (units of 2 s; reset 10 per Milan 5.6.2 ⇒ 20 s validity) is 🟡 **WRITE-ONLY SCRATCH** -- the processor holds valid_time as an internal constant and the ADPDU carries that, not this

ADP_ECAPS.name: Entity capabilities (scratch)
ADP_ECAPS.purpose: Stored and read back; the processor supplies the ADPDU field.

fields.ADP_ENTITY_CAPS: 🟡 **WRITE-ONLY SCRATCH**: entity_capabilities (e.g. `0xC588` for a Milan PAAD). Stored and read back; the ADPDU carries the processor's internal constant (`ADP_ENTITY_CAPS_C` in `pp_adp_pkg.sv`). Writing it changes nothing observable. **Nothing writes it**: the bare-metal firmware no longer writes its stale `0x8588` copy (#398), so the word reads back its reset `0`

I2SPB_STAT.name: I2S playback drift rails
I2SPB_STAT.purpose: Underrun and overrun counts, each half cleared on write.

fields.UNDERRUN: Underrun count. Any set bit written here restarts this whole half, not only the set bits.
fields.OVERRUN: Overrun count. Any set bit written here restarts this whole half, not only the set bits.

fields.TONE_ENABLE: pilot tone enable: 1 kHz exact-period 48×24-bit sine replaces the I2S ADC on both talker channels (digital THD+N −148.1 dB; E2E acceptance ≤ −120 dBFS at the physical Listener output).
fields.TONE_ATT: **attenuation**, −6 dB steps applied as `TONE_TAB_C[idx] >>> att` (0 = 0 dBFS full scale, 7 = −42 dB); reset is `0`, so the power-on tone is 0 dBFS and any smaller amplitude was dialled in at the bench. A capture at amplitude 0.25 means `att = 2`, not a quarter-scale table: `8388607 >>> 2 = 2097151`, and `2097151 / 2^23 = 0.24999988`. Reduce before measuring through a sample-rate conversion or an analog stage, because a 0 dBFS sampled sine overshoots between samples (measured +0.91 dB through a 48 kHz to 44.1 kHz conversion) and would clip; at 48 kHz end to end the maxima land on table entries and 0 dBFS is safe. See the [obsolete historical media-clock finding](docs/history/v1/findings/MEDIA_CLOCK_LOCK_0810.md)

fields.CRF_LOCKED: locked (RO live). Eight clean consecutive PDUs establish lock. No consumed accepted PDU for 100 ms clears lock. So does an unbind (enable and ACMP bind both low). Each counts one MEDIA_UNLOCKED (#653). A profile validation error retains lock and breaks settling. It does not refresh the timeout. Each observation interval containing errors increments `UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT` (`fmt_err_o`) once. `CRF_STATUS[15:8]` (`0x74C`) exposes its low eight bits. GET_COUNTERS exposes all 32 bits.

STRMW_CNT.name: Stream window counter
STRMW_CNT.purpose: One of the ten snapshot-latched Stream Input counters.

fields.SNAP_SHADOW: The 10 Milan Table 5.6 / 1722.1-2021 Table 7-157 STREAM_INPUT counters at the Table 7-157 word offsets 0..36: MEDIA_LOCKED, MEDIA_UNLOCKED, STREAM_INTERRUPTED, SEQ_NUM_MISMATCH, MEDIA_RESET, TIMESTAMP_UNCERTAIN, UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT, LATE_TIMESTAMP, EARLY_TIMESTAMP, FRAMES_RX. **Full 32-bit** -- this is the authoritative width; the flat `AVTPRX_STAT`/`AVTPRX_ERR` words are saturating 8/16-bit summaries of these. Until VERSION `0x0013` the index-0 words were re-derived from those packed views and inherited their truncation (and MEDIA_RESET / LATE / EARLY_TIMESTAMP read a hard 0 while the monitor was counting them), so there was **no** full-width path anywhere. Talker contexts read `0xDEADDEAD` (the not-backed rule below). **The two Milan 1.3 5.3.8.10 additions -- TIMESTAMP_VALID / TIMESTAMP_NOT_VALID (per-frame tv-bit tallies, LCTX words 26/27, `TV + TNV == FRAMES_RX`) -- are NOT window-exposed** (the `0x858+` words were already claimed); they are served by AECP GET_COUNTERS at the 1722.1-2021 block offsets 24/28 under valid mask `0xFFF` (was `0xF3F`), and a bench read can fetch LCTX w26/w27 through the raw `lctx` read port if ever needed

fields.STRMW_PDUS: listener: `{drops[31:16], pdus[15:0]}` (= `PCMRX_CNT` at idx 0); talker: per-stream frames_sent (idx 0 = `AAF_FRAMES`; idx>0 = the packetizer ctx FRAMES word, snap-fetched through the TCTX port)

fields.STRMW_SRP: 🔴 **STRUCTURAL ZERO at every index.** There is no lwSRP attribute-row table in this fabric any more, so the window's SRP port is never granted and this word reads 0 -- including at idx 0, whose live hard alias of `LWSRP_STATUS` (`0x694`) went with the port. Read `LWSRP_STATUS` `0x694` directly instead: it carries the processor's class-D declaration/registration levels for the whole plane. Was: `{valid, dir, declared, registered, ready, failed, decl[1:0], fail_code[7:0]}` from the selected context row, with `0xDEAD` for a row above `N_CTX_P`

PP_CTRL.purpose: Entity enable and the restore-walk start.

fields.PP_ENABLE: **entity enable**, ORed with `ADP_CTRL[0]` (`0x600`); either bit starts the plane.
fields.PP_RESTORE_GO: `restore_go`: start the NVM boot-restore walk against the saved-state backing store (`KL_nvm_backend` behind the processor's NVM device face, [design page](docs/design/SAVED_STATE_FASTCONNECT.md) sections 4, 8 and 9). Until firmware has configured AND validated a record image through `PP_NVM_SEL`/`PP_NVM_DATA` the face answers blank flash (reads `0xFF`, writes accepted and discarded, erase completes), so the walk completes with **zero records** and `restore_fail` set. **Validate the image first, then set this bit**: the verdict is latched per walk, and validating afterwards restores nothing. **Set it on every boot** (processor pin `a8f8ce81`, its issue 92): the processor holds its ACMP listener from reset until the walk ends, so a boot that never sets it never answers an ACMP listener command. Since processor pin `d352bbaa` it also holds AECP until the D3 walk's terminal, and that walk proves the AEM image first: **load and CRC-check the AEM image before this bit**, or the restore ends CLOSED (`PP_STAT[16]`) and AECP stays held until reset. Every restore wait is bounded by `NVM_RS_TMO_CYC_P` (20 ms) and the whole restore by `NVM_RS_AGG_CYC_P` (1,000 ms from this bit), both derived from the clock, so a device face that never answers ends the walks with `restore_fail` set; wait for `restore_done` OR `PP_STAT[16]`, since CLOSED never raises done

PP_STAT.name: Processor status
PP_STAT.purpose: Presence tag, saved-state verdict and side-port status.

PP_SPADDR.name: Processor side-port address
PP_SPADDR.purpose: Side-port word address; a write posts a read.

PP_SPDATA.name: Processor side-port data
PP_SPDATA.purpose: Posted read data; a write posts a side-port write.

fields.PP_SPRDATA: **Read**: the data of the last posted read. **Write**: posts a side-port WRITE of this value to the address already in `PP_SPADDR` (ignored while `sp_busy`)

PP_DIAG.name: Processor frame diagnostics
PP_DIAG.purpose: Control frames sent, received and dropped.

PP_NVM_SEL.name: Saved-state window select
PP_NVM_SEL.purpose: Index of the backend word PP_NVM_DATA reads or writes.

fields.PP_NVM_CSR_RDATA: the word `PP_NVM_SEL` names. Words `0`-`3` and both tables read back what was written; word `4` reads `0` (strobes have no state to read); words `5` and `8`-`15` are read-only fabric state

PP_NVM_STAT.name: Saved-state status and strobes
PP_NVM_STAT.purpose: Backend status word on read, strobe word on write.

STRMW_RSVD_86C.name: Stream window hole
STRMW_RSVD_86C.purpose: An undefined word of the stream window.

win_in_range_w: the selected stream does not exist
acmp_fresh_r: the ACMP table answered since the last selection
the ACMP table has not answered since the last selection
srp_fresh_r: the SRP table answered since the last selection
the SRP table has not answered since the last selection
stg_hit_w: the staged identity belongs to the selected stream
the staged identity belongs to another stream
srp_idx0_ls_w: `STRM_SEL[9]` selects the listener row at index 0
`STRM_SEL[9]` does not select the listener row at index 0
condition_words.snap_kind_r: the kind the last snapshot recorded for this counter
